extracted.intended_audience: Canadian patent applicants, patentees, and their representatives (patent agents and registered foreign practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative and compliance requirements for establishing filing/presentation dates, divisional and PCT national-phase entries, required parts, translations, fees, notices, and representation under the Canadian Patent Act and Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation required for documents not in English or French (subsection 15(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submitted document is partly or entirely in a language other than English or French, the applicant must submit an English or French translation when required under the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the translation is not provided on the filing date, the Commissioner will send a notice under subsection 15(4) requiring submission of the translated document within two months of the notice. If the translation is submitted within two months it replaces the original; failure to submit within the prescribed time will result in the application being deemed abandoned under subsection 73(2) of the Patent Act (as prescribed by subsection 132(1)(a) of the Patent Rules). See related notice procedures in Chapter 9 for abandonment and reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference statement in lieu of description (subsection 27.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a reference statement to the Commissioner instead of the description to secure a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference statement must be in English or French and state that a reference to a specified previously filed application is being submitted instead of all or part of the specification or drawing required in the application. A reference statement cannot be used to secure a filing date for a divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to make a complete reference statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescribed period to make a complete reference statement begins on the date the Office receives any document to establish a filing date and ends the earlier of specified deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines: (a) two months from receipt of the earliest document (or, if a notice under subsection 28(2) is sent, the earlier of two months after the notice and six months after receipt); and (b) the filing date. Meet these timelines to secure the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of a reference statement (paragraph 67(2)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference statement must include particulars about the previously filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the name of the country/office of filing and either the number of the previously filed application or, if unknown, one of: the provisional number given by that office; the date it was sent to that office (accompanied by a copy of the request portion); or the applicant’s reference number plus applicant name/address, title of invention and date sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and method for providing copy of previously filed application (paragraph 67(2)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant has two months from the date the reference statement was submitted to provide a copy of the previously filed application or make it available in an acceptable digital library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the previously filed application was filed in Canada, the applicant is exempted from providing a copy. If all requirements are met, the specification/drawings in the previously filed application are deemed to have been contained in the Canadian application on the date the statement was received; filing date is the latest of dates when documents under section 71 were submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of previously filed application not in English or French (subsection 15(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a previously filed application is in a language other than English or French, the applicant must provide an English or French translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation is not submitted with the copy, the Commissioner will issue a notice under subsection 15(4) requiring translation within two months. Timely submission replaces the original; failure leads to abandonment under subsection 73(2) as prescribed by subsection 132(1)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition to specification or drawings (section 28.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the wrong specification/drawings were filed or part was omitted, an addition may be possible under section 28.01 within a narrow timeframe, but it may affect filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the addition together with a statement indicating it is made under section 28.01. Because of tight timelines and potential filing date effects, applicants are encouraged to ensure submissions establishing a filing date are complete and error-free and to include a summary list of application parts to help Office reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for making an addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants have two months from the earliest date the Commissioner received any document/information required for a filing date to add the missing part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioner notifies the applicant of a missing part, the addition must be made before the earlier of: (i) two months after the date of the notice; and (ii) six months after the date the Commissioner received any document/information under subsection 28(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to preserve original filing date when adding missing parts (subsection 28.01(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: To secure the original filing date when adding missing matter, the addition must be completely contained in a prior application on which priority has been requested, and additional conditions must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: (1) a request for priority in respect of that prior application was made on the earliest date the Commissioner received any document/information; (2) the addition is completely contained in that prior application; (3) the applicant requests that the filing date be the earlier filing date; and (4) compliance with any other prescribed requirements. If the prior application was not filed in Canada, provide a copy or make it available in an acceptable digital library and provide translations of parts not in English/French, indicating where the addition is contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on filing date if added parts are not contained in priority application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the parts being added are not contained in a prior application on which priority has been requested (and the request is not withdrawn), the filing date will be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing date will be the later of the date on which the addition is received and the filing date (where other filing requirements have not been met); an amended filing certificate results. The Office will expedite assessment so applicants have the opportunity to withdraw the addition and maintain the original filing date where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee timing and consequences (subsection 27(7) & 66(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application fee is not required to establish a filing date, but must be paid when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unpaid on the filing date, the Commissioner will notify the applicant that the application fee and late payment fee must be paid within three months of the notice. Failure to pay within that period leads to the application being considered withdrawn. Small entity applicants may pay reduced fees upon meeting conditions and submitting a small entity declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of unique application number at filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application is assigned a unique application number once a filing date is established; applications and any resulting patent bear the same number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications receive a number distinct from the original application; reissued and re-examined patents retain the original number. Historical numbering details noted for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: After required documents/information are submitted and a filing date established, the Commissioner will send a filing certificate with a unique application number to the default correspondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 5 for default correspondent information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of an application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be withdrawn at any time by written request from a person authorized to represent the applicant(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application fee referred to in subsection 27(2) is not refundable. Other fees paid prior to withdrawal may be refundable under paragraph 139(1)(b) of the Patent Rules. For information on representation, see Chapter 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry in Canada (section 154)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international PCT application may enter the Canadian national phase upon meeting requirements in section 154 of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once entered, the application is considered filed in Canada on its national entry date; the international filing date becomes its filing date in Canada and prosecution continues under the Patent Act and Rules. Many PCT national phase applications may already be administratively compliant on entry (see 4.01.01). See Chapter 34 for more PCT details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application definition and filing date benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application is a separate patent application divided from an original application that describes more than one invention and benefits from the same filing date as the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications are separate for most purposes and require separate fees. The Manual describes administrative filing requirements for divisionals in subsequent sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'original application' for divisionals (subsection 36(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional is deemed separate and distinct; the Act's provisions apply fully and separate fees are payable; except for some provisions, it has the same filing date as the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisional may itself be considered an original application for the purposes of filing further divisionals (i.e., grandparent → parent → child divisionals are possible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation-date requirements to file a divisional (section 89 & 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: To file a divisional, the applicant must meet the majority of section 89 requirements on the presentation date set out in section 103; many presentation-date requirements mirror filing-date requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish a presentation date the submission must include: an explicit/implicit request for a patent; applicant identity information; contact information for the Commissioner to contact the applicant; and a document that appears to be a description. For divisionals the description must be in English or French (subsection 15(1)). Additional section 89 requirements: petition including a statement that the application is a divisional; original application number submitted not later than three months after presentation date; at least one applicant must have been an applicant on the original application during the required period; the application must contain one or more claims on its presentation date; and any required translations for the original application must have been provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original application number submission (divisional) — after presentation date
rubrics_metrics.description: An original application number may be provided after the presentation date, but the Office cannot process the divisional until it is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: provide the original application number on the presentation date. If an incorrect original number was provided, the correct number may be submitted not later than three months after the presentation date and Office records will be updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include full subject matter for divisionals on presentation date
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office recommends including all subject matter relevant to the invention permitted under section 91 or 155.7 on the presentation date of a divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All future amendments to the specification and drawings of the divisional will be assessed based on the subject matter submitted on the presentation date. For evaluation of new subject matter during examination, see Chapter 20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee requirement for divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each divisional requires payment of the application fee, although the fee is not required to establish the filing of a divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee is not submitted on the presentation date, the Commissioner will send a notice under subsection 27(7) requiring payment of the fee and late fee within three months of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees for divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees for divisional applications are separate from the original application and are calculated from the filing date of the original application; they are payable at the presentation date of the divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if divisional is filed 40 months after original filing, maintenance fees for the 2nd and 3rd anniversaries must be paid on presentation. If required maintenance fees are not paid, the Commissioner will send a notice requiring payment before the later of two months from the notice or six months from presentation; a single late fee applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to meet section 89 requirements on presentation date (consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for the original application number, the applicant must meet section 89 requirements on the presentation date for the application to be a divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requirements (other than original number) are not met on presentation date, the presentation date becomes the filing date and the application will be treated as a regularly filed application; the Office will send a filing certificate for a regular application. Applicant may withdraw the regular application and re-file as a divisional if requirements can be met on the same date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline constraints for filing divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional cannot be filed if the original application has been granted or abandoned beyond the period of reinstatement; divisionals may be filed after the original has been refused if within the time prescribed in section 90.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attempt to file a divisional after the deadline but that otherwise meets filing date requirements will be treated as a regular application and a filing certificate issued accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions deemed taken for divisionals (section 92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain actions taken in respect of the original application before the presentation date are deemed to have been taken for the divisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deemed actions include: small entity declaration filed; request for priority made and not withdrawn; information under subsection 28.4(2) submitted; a copy or English/French translation of a previously regularly filed application submitted; copy made available in digital library; information for deposit of biological material submitted; requests under subsection 95(1) submitted. The Office will ensure divisional records reflect these actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original-application notices continue to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not comply with a notice sent with respect to the original application before the presentation date, that notice will continue to apply to the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisional will be independently assessed for compliance and will be subject to separate notices where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public inspection of divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a divisional is filed after the expiry of the eighteen-month confidentiality period of the original application, the divisional and documents filed with it are open to public inspection immediately upon filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The confidentiality period of a divisional is calculated based on the earliest filing date of any previously filed application on which a request for priority is made in respect of the divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required parts of a compliant patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: A compliant patent application must contain certain parts in order to be compliant with the Patent Act and Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required parts: a petition conforming with section 53 of the Patent Rules; the name and postal address of each inventor; a statement of entitlement or inventorship; a claim or claims; an abstract; drawings if applicable; and a sequence listing that complies with the PCT sequence listing standard if applicable. Other administrative requirements (e.g., application fee, agent appointment) are assessed elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliant PCT national phase applications (administrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information/notices included with an international application as filed or furnished under the PCT before national phase entry are deemed received by the Commissioner on the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, many PCT national phase applications are already administratively compliant on the national phase entry date. See section 4.01.01 and Chapter 34 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of non-compliance after filing (section 65)
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing, the Office reviews whether required parts have been submitted and will issue a notice under section 65 if required parts (other than sequence listings or drawings) are missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant has three months to respond in good faith to avoid abandonment under subsection 73(2). After required parts are submitted, specification, claims, abstract and drawings are not thoroughly assessed until examination and may receive defect reports then. PCT national phase translation requirements are assessed on national phase entry; notice under subsection 155.5(6) may be issued for missing translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Commissioner’s notice of non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office reviews the applicant’s response to a notice under section 65 and assesses whether the response renders the application compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application remains non‑compliant, a new notice under section 65 will be sent and the applicant will again have three months to respond in good faith to avoid abandonment. For subsection 155.5(6) notices, failure to comply may cause abandonment under subsection 132(1)(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirement (section 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application (except PCT national phase applications) must contain a petition that complies with section 53 of the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may include other information in the petition such as a small entity declaration, request for priority, entitlement information per section 54, and appointments of common representative or patent agent. Applicants may use the provided form or their own petition form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor information and entitlement statements (subsection 54(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must indicate the name and postal address of each inventor and include statements establishing entitlement to apply and inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: a statement that the applicant(s) are entitled to apply for a patent; a statement that the applicant is sole inventor or that joint applicants are all inventors; for PCT national phase, a declaration per Rule 4.17(ii) if applicable. These statements must be in the petition or submitted in a document other than the abstract, specification, or drawings. If missing on filing date, Commissioner will send a section 65 notice requiring the missing information within three months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: submission and notice procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings appear intended but are missing on the filing date, the applicant will be notified by a Commissioner’s notice under subsection 72(1) (unless PCT national phase or divisional, where a courtesy letter is sent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During examination, the examiner may identify that drawings are required to make the application compliant and will state this in the examiner’s report (see chapter 12.05.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sequence listing appears intended but missing at filing, the Office will notify the applicant (notice under subsection 72(1) or courtesy letter for PCT/divisional). Sequence listings must comply with the PCT sequence listing standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliant listings will trigger a section 65 notice or an examiner’s requisition. If a listing is added later under subsection 58(3), the applicant must file a statement that the listing does not add matter beyond the disclosure in the application as filed. Examiners may require sequence listings in reports (see chapter 23.05.07a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement when a description or previously filed application is not in English/French
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submitted description or previously filed application is partly or entirely in a language other than English or French, a translation into English or French must be provided to the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reiterates the translation obligations (see 4.07 and 4.08); if missing on filing date the Commissioner will issue a subsection 15(4) notice requiring translation within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requiring translation (subsection 15(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a required translation is not provided on filing, the Commissioner issues a notice requiring translation submission within two months from the notice date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely translation replaces the original document; failure to submit within the prescribed time results in abandonment under subsection 73(2) as prescribed by subsection 132(1)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: General formatting and presentation requirements (sections 47–52)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description, claims, abstract and drawings must be presented to allow the Patent Office to process, scan and read them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Rules set out page margins, line numbering, line spacing, font size, page numbering and identification of trademarks. Each part of the application must begin on a new page; other requirements concerning drawings and formulas must be met. Non-compliance may be identified in an Office letter or an examiner’s report. See chapter 2.02.02 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and use of patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent agents holding licences from the College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents may represent applicants, patentees and clients before the Patent Office; the Office recommends consulting a licensed patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Register of Patent Agents is maintained by the College; requirements to obtain/maintain licences are set by the College which may suspend or revoke licences. The Patent Office relies on College updates but agents must notify the Office of address/method-of-correspondence changes to avoid errors (see 5.02.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered foreign practitioners — limitations and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered foreign practitioners are persons recognized under laws of other countries with limited ability to act before the Canadian Patent Office and are not considered 'patent agents' under the Patent Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To act on behalf of an applicant/patentee, a registered foreign practitioner must be explicitly permitted under the Patent Rules to take the requested action, must be authorized by the applicant/patentee, and must be listed on the College’s list of registered foreign practitioners. Consult chapters 5.05 and 5.07 for permitted actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative for joint applicants/patentees
rubrics_metrics.description: A common representative is a joint applicant or joint patentee entitled to act on behalf of the other joint applicants or patentees in certain actions before the Office, including appointment of patent agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there are joint applicants/patentees, one will be the common representative; joint applicants/patentees may collectively appoint a common representative. See Chapter 5 for representation rules and appointments.
